title: Improve client-facing error for streaming disconnects (request IDs + retry guidance)
creator: Dev Patel
project: CS & Support Escalation Playbook Refresh / Known-Issues Sprint (2026-02)
description:
Problem
Support is spending significant time on back-and-forth when customers report streaming disconnects (mid-generation stream reset / truncated output). Today the client often sees a generic network-ish error (or an unhelpful 5xx) without:
- a stable request identifier to share with Support
- clear classification (client disconnect vs gateway idle timeout vs upstream runtime reset)
- safe, copy/paste retry guidance (including idempotency guidance for streaming)

This is showing up repeatedly in escalations and is a top known-issues sprint item (see SUP-1842, SUP-1854). The goal is to make the *first* customer report contain enough signal to triage quickly and, where appropriate, enable the customer to self-mitigate via documented retry/timeouts.

Goals
1) Include a request ID in streaming-disconnect responses in a way customers can reliably capture and paste into Support.
2) Improve error classification and message text so customers can distinguish: retryable transient vs likely client/proxy timeout vs configuration issue.
3) Add minimal retry guidance inline (and/or link to docs) without over-promising or exposing internal implementation details.
4) Reduce Support time-to-triage and time-to-mitigation for streaming disconnect tickets.

Non-goals
- Redesign streaming protocol behavior.
- Implement full client-side retry libraries in the server.
- Expose internal incident details or customer-sensitive routing info.

Proposed changes (server-side)
A) Request ID propagation
- Ensure every streaming request has a request_id generated at the gateway edge (if not provided) and propagated through to runtime logs.
- Return request ID to clients consistently:
  - Response header: x-redwood-request-id: <id>
  - For streaming: on error termination, include request_id in the final error payload (where the protocol supports it).

B) Standardized error code + message
Introduce/standardize a small set of public-facing error codes for streaming termination cases (names TBD, but must be stable across SDKs):
- STREAM_DISCONNECT_RETRYABLE (e.g., upstream reset / transient gateway failure)
- STREAM_TIMEOUT_IDLE (likely idle timeout between chunks; advise keepalive/timeout tuning)
- STREAM_CLIENT_CLOSED (client closed connection; not actionable on server)
- STREAM_UPSTREAM_OVERLOADED (capacity/transient; advise retry with backoff)

For each, return:
- code (stable)
- message (customer-safe)
- request_id
- retryable: true/false
- recommended_action (short string, e.g., "retry_with_backoff" | "increase_client_timeout" | "capture_request_id_and_contact_support")

C) Minimal inline retry guidance
For retryable errors, include 1–2 sentences max in the message, aligned with Docs/Support wording:
- Suggest exponential backoff + jitter
- Recommend setting an explicit client read timeout appropriate for long generations
- Recommend capturing request ID and timestamps if it persists

Important: Avoid giving guidance that could cause duplicate side effects. For streaming, we should explicitly call out that customers should use idempotency keys where supported, or only auto-retry requests that are safe for their app logic.

D) Observability alignment
- Make sure request_id is present in gateway logs and the on-call dashboards Support uses (ties into ENG-4821 metrics clarity).

Customer-facing copy constraints
- Do not mention specific regions/providers/hosts.
- Do not reference internal service names.
- Do not imply an SLA credit outcome.
- Keep guidance consistent with the published workaround article: "Streaming timeouts and reconnect".

Acceptance criteria
- For a forced streaming disconnect test case, the customer receives an error that includes request_id (header + payload where applicable).
- Support can locate the request in logs by request_id without requesting additional correlating info in the common case.
- Error payload includes a stable code and retryable boolean.
- Copy is reviewed by Support + Docs for customer-safe wording.
- Backward compatibility: existing clients that don’t parse the new fields continue to function.

Rollout plan
- Ship behind a feature flag at the gateway.
- Enable for internal accounts + Support test tenants first.
- Gradual ramp (e.g., 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with monitoring on:
  - rate of streaming error classifications
  - client error rates
  - Support ticket volume tagged "streaming disconnect"

References / links
- Support tickets: SUP-1842 (streaming connection resets us-east), SUP-1854 (streaming response truncated mid-token)
- Docs: workaround-streaming-timeouts-and-reconnect (Known Issues)
- GitHub PR (implementation): sources/github/redwood/pr-19321-improve-streaming-disconnect-error-details.json
- Related work:
  - ENG-4821 add support signal to routing/fallback metrics
  - ENG-4830 incident bot Jira linking for SUP tickets

Open questions
- Final list of public error codes (coordinate with SDK maintainers so naming is consistent across Python/TS/Go).
- For streaming protocols: confirm the best place to surface payload error metadata (SSE event vs trailer vs JSON terminal message), without breaking existing SDK stream iterators.
- Confirm whether we should expose retry-after for overloaded cases (may help but must be accurate).

Risks
- Breaking changes if SDKs make assumptions about terminal stream frames.
- Over-encouraging retries could amplify load during incidents; keep guidance conservative and aligned with on-call/SRE.

Owner
Mina Haddad (with review from Support + Docs).
comments: 2026-02-04 (Dev Patel): Creating per known-issues sprint. Streaming escalations keep stalling because customers can’t provide request IDs. Need customer-visible request_id + retryable classification so Support can route quickly without multiple follow-ups.

2026-02-06 (Sean Gallagher): +1. Please ensure retry guidance doesn’t encourage aggressive loops during degradations. Prefer explicit retryable boolean and conservative wording. Also align codes with alerting categories so on-call can map quickly.
2026-02-07 (Elliot Price): Docs can mirror whatever stable code list we land on. Strong preference: keep message short, point to troubleshooting page for details. Avoid region/provider mention.

2026-02-10 (Owen Phillips): From recent bridge: customers were retrying streaming immediately with no backoff and caused bursts. Suggest including backoff language and pointing to idempotency guidance. Request ID in header is critical; many clients only capture headers.

2026-02-12 (Mina Haddad): Implementation in progress via PR-19321. Plan: generate request_id at edge if missing; return x-redwood-request-id always; add structured error with code/retryable. Need SDK owners to confirm they expose header values on streaming exceptions.

2026-02-14 (Wei Chen): Reviewed draft messages; recommend removing the word “overloaded” and instead say “temporary capacity or network interruption” to avoid implying capacity guarantees. Add 'If this persists, contact Support with request ID and approx timestamp'.

2026-02-16 (Mina Haddad): PR up for review. Added unit tests for header propagation and error mapping. Pending: final error code naming and Docs sign-off on copy. Targeting runtime-1.18.x patch train.
